tasks.title: Create shared issue template artifact and lookup utility
tasks.description: Add `packages/cli/src/agent-skills/issue-templates.md` as the single source of truth for issue authoring guidance, with stable sections for user-story, refactor, design, docs, and UI templates. Add a small lookup/parser utility that maps supported labels to template sections so both the CLI and shared skill installation can read the same artifact deterministically.
acceptanceCriteria: `packages/cli/src/agent-skills/issue-templates.md` exists and contains exactly five template groups covering `bug`/`feature`/`improvement`, `refactor`, `design`, `docs`, and `ui-feature`/`ui-improvement`
The UI template includes a required ASCII prototype section, a box-layout example, and guidance for representing interaction/state changes

The lookup utility resolves `bug`, `feature`, and `improvement` to the shared user-story template and resolves `refactor`, `design`, `docs`, `ui-feature`, and `ui-improvement` to their correct template groups
The parser fails clearly or returns no match for unknown labels instead of silently falling back to the wrong template
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/src/agent-skills/issue-templates.md and supporting template lookup utility under packages/cli/src/agent-skills/
tasks.notes: Keep the markdown human-editable and use a minimal section format such as stable headings plus label metadata so the same artifact can be consumed without duplicating strings in TypeScript.

tasks.title: Add `mo instructions` command for template discovery and output
tasks.description: Register a new top-level `mo instructions` command that reads the shared template artifact locally, lists available template groups when called without arguments, and prints the matching template when called with a supported label. The command should stay server-independent, normalize labels through the lookup utility, and return a non-zero error for unsupported labels while showing valid choices.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo instructions` prints the available template groups and the labels served by each group
`mo instructions refactor` outputs the technical refactor template instead of the user-story template
`mo instructions ui-feature` outputs the UI template including the ASCII prototype requirement
Unsupported labels exit with a non-zero status and print the valid labels
The command does not require `mo server` to be running and does not call server-only command helpers
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Consumes the artifact and label mapping introduced in T-001. Prefer raw markdown output for the selected template so the result is easy to pipe or copy into issue authoring flows.

tasks.title: Thin the shared `mohist` skill and align it with AgentSkills structure
tasks.description: Rewrite `packages/cli/src/agent-skills/templates/mohist.md` so it keeps command reference, label/priority guidance, and template-selection rules, but removes the embedded full issue body template. The skill should explicitly direct users and agents to run `mo instructions <label>` and remain compliant with the AgentSkills specification through minimal, valid frontmatter and clear executable guidance.
acceptanceCriteria: The `mohist` skill frontmatter remains valid and includes a stable `name` and concise `description`
The skill no longer embeds the full five-step issue template or duplicate full template bodies
The skill tells users and agents to run `mo instructions <label>` before writing or revising an issue body
The skill still documents supported labels, including `refactor`, and no longer forces refactor issues into a user-story-only shape
The skill mentions the installed companion template artifact so local reference still works after installation
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 for the shared template contract and T-002 because the skill should point at the real command users will run. Preserve existing operational guidance for non-template CLI actions.

tasks.title: Refactor shared skill installation to ship companion template files
tasks.description: Change shared skill installation from implicit markdown-file scanning to an explicit shared-skill bundle manifest so Mohist can install `SKILL.md` plus companion files. Ensure `mohist` installs both `SKILL.md` and `issue-templates.md`, `mohist-explore` still installs only `SKILL.md`, and `mo skills list` continues to report shared skill names rather than companion artifacts.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo skills install` writes `.agents/skills/mohist/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/mohist/issue-templates.md` from the shared source files
`mo skills install` still writes `.agents/skills/mohist-explore/SKILL.md` and does not treat `issue-templates.md` as a separate skill
The installer continues to support the Claude target directory behavior without changing the shared skill names it reports
`mo skills list` still lists `mohist` and `mohist-explore` rather than companion files
The installed `issue-templates.md` content matches the single source artifact used by `mo instructions`
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Consumes T-001 because the installed companion file must come from the shared artifact, and T-003 because the installed `mohist` skill content changes together with the bundle layout. Keep the manifest minimal to avoid a larger skill packaging migration.

tasks.title: Add regression coverage for instructions output and bundled skill installation
tasks.description: Add focused automated tests covering template listing, per-label output, UI ASCII prototype guidance, and multi-file shared skill installation. The regression suite should prove the CLI, shared artifact, and installer stay aligned and that existing `mohist` and `mohist-explore` behavior is not broken by the new bundling model.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests verify `mo instructions` lists available template groups and prints the correct template for `refactor` and at least one UI label
Tests verify unknown labels fail with a helpful error that includes valid labels
Tests verify the UI template output contains the ASCII prototype requirement and example content
Tests verify shared skill installation writes `mohist/SKILL.md`, `mohist/issue-templates.md`, and `mohist-explore/SKILL.md` to the expected target directory
Tests verify `mo skills list` continues to expose only shared skill names, not companion files
Tests pass: `cd packages/cli && npm test`
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/tests/shared-agent-skills.test.ts, packages/cli/tests/cli-commands.test.ts, and/or focused new CLI test files
tasks.notes: This final regression task consumes every earlier output: the shared artifact, the new CLI command, the thinned skill, and the installer bundle behavior. Prefer focused tests near existing shared-skill and CLI command coverage rather than broad end-to-end scenarios.
